reading.body:
At 1.37 MW of published IT capacity across 33,135 square feet of technical space, this campus is a small facility by any measure relevant to AI. Assuming 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 1.37 MW supports roughly 34 racks, at that assumption about 34 × 40 kW = 1,360 kW. At the lower inference density of 10 kW per rack, the same power reaches roughly 137 racks. Either way, the footprint is more consistent with enterprise colocation or inference at modest scale than with large-model training, which routinely consumes tens or hundreds of megawatts in a single cluster.

The certification stack tells a clear story about the intended customer profile. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 qualify the facility for audited financial and operational controls. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment-card workloads. ITAR qualifies it for controlled defense and export-regulated data. HITRUST qualifies it for regulated healthcare information. NIST 800-53 qualifies it for federal security control frameworks. Together these certifications point toward compliance-sensitive enterprise workloads, not high-density AI compute.

Within Nevada, this site ranks second by published IT capacity among the two facilities on this site that carry a published megawatt figure, out of 26 mapped facilities in the state total. Its 1.37 MW represents roughly 13 percent of the 10.37 MW this site has read from Nevada operator pages, a share that reflects how narrow the published-data sample is, not necessarily the state's true installed base. Nevada's grid and land constraints are not published on this operator's spec page and are therefore not assessed here.
